name: closeyourit-nuxt3-proof
//: @simple-git/argv-parser 1.1.1 has a critical flaw: the check simple-git uses to block dangerous
Git options does not recognise include.path, submodule.<name>.update, url.<base>.insteadOf,
--exec-path and the replacement of internal binaries, so it lets command execution through.
Fixed from 2.0.1. It comes from simple-git 3.36.0 (latest 3.x, accepts only ^1.1.0), via
@nuxt/devtools 3.4.x which nuxt 3.21.11 requires: development panel only, it does not end up in the
example's build nor in the published package. No stable version of @nuxt/devtools accepts
simple-git 4, so 2.0.1 is forced (same vulnerabilityCheck API), as in the Nuxt 4 example.
When devtools updates the override must be removed by hand. See CYJS-49 and CYJS-50.
node-forge 1.4.0 has a known flaw and no fixed version exists yet. It comes only from
listhen, the development server that @nuxt/cli and nitropack include, and it is only used to create
the certificates of the HTTPS development server, which the Nuxt smoke does not start. It is replaced
with the local empty package vendor/node-forge: it loads without errors and fails with a clear
message as soon as someone uses it. It does not end up in the published package. When a fixed
version of node-forge is out the override and the vendor folder must be removed by hand. See CYJS-54.
braces 3.0.3 stays vulnerable by choice (accepted risk): a path pattern with deeply nested braces
can exhaust resources during expansion and block the process. It comes from
micromatch 4.0.8 via fast-glob 3.3.3 and globby 16.x, which nitropack 2.13.4 uses to look up files
only while it prepares and builds the example: it does not run in the started server nor end up in
the published package. No version of braces fixes the flaw yet, so an override would not help
and the lockfile stays as it is. To be rechecked as soon as a fixed version of braces is out: at
that point it is updated and this note must be removed, as in the Nuxt 4 example. See CYJS-51 and CYJS-52.
simple-git 3.36.0 stays vulnerable by choice (accepted risk) to three flaws: the check on dangerous
Git options is bypassed with abbreviated long options (--receive-p, --exe) and lets commands
run (fixed from 4.0.0); Git configuration includes are not blocked and
also allow running commands (GHSA-g4wm-2vf7-vfgr, fixed from 4.0.0); the check
does not block the trailer.<name>.command / .cmd configuration, which makes Git run a command
(GHSA-x6jw-m9v5-85vh, CVE-2026-102828, fixed from 4.0.1).
For includes (GHSA-g4wm-2vf7-vfgr, CVE-2026-102826) the main path is already closed: simple-git
delegates the check to @simple-git/argv-parser, forced above to 2.0.1, which rejects both
include.path and includeIf.<condition>.path without allowUnsafeInclude. The secondary path stays
open: by changing HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME Git is made to read a configuration chosen by someone else,
which the check does not inspect. The panel runs only on the developer's computer and receives no
external data, so the risk stays accepted.
It comes from @nuxt/devtools 3.4.2 (requires ^3.36.0), the development panel that nuxt 3.21.11
requires (^3.4.1): it is not needed by the built site nor ends up in the published package. Forcing
simple-git 4 breaks the devtools postinstall (4 no longer has the default export), so no
override and the lockfile stays as it is. No stable version of @nuxt/devtools accepts simple-git 4.
To be rechecked as soon as nuxt requires a stable version of @nuxt/devtools that accepts simple-git 4
or no longer uses it: at that point it is updated (at least to 4.0.1) and this note must be removed, as
in the Nuxt 4 example. See CYJS-55, CYJS-56, CYJS-57, CYJS-58 and CYJS-59.
